definition: Gerard A. "Gerry" Salton (8 March 1927 – 28 August 1995) was a professor of computer science at Cornell University.
details: Salton was perhaps the leading computer scientist working in the field of information retrieval during his time, and "the father of Information Retrieval". His group at Cornell developed the SMART Information Retrieval System, which he initiated when he was at Harvard. It was the first system to use the now popular vector space model for information retrieval.

explainer.lead: Gerard Salton was an American computer scientist (1927-1995). His work spans information retrieval.
explainer.knownFor: Salton was perhaps most well known for developing the now widely used vector space model for Information Retrieval.

contributions.name: He received a Bachelor's (1950) and Master's (1952) degree in mathematics from Brooklyn College, and a Ph.D. from Harvard in applied mathematics in 1958, the last of Howard Aiken's doctoral students, and taught there until 1965, when he joined Cornell University and co-founded its department of Computer Science.

affiliations: Harvard School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
